meta.title: Agrokruh / Arbolis crop slate v1
meta.climate: temperate–continental outdoor, Czech-like (cold winters, warm summers, frost risk)
meta.yieldFraming: Mid-typical intensive / market-garden fresh yields where relevant; perennials use annual productive harvest not standing woody biomass
meta.nutrientQualityScale: nutrientQuality.score1to5 is a game-facing composite (1–5) of the edible portion: (1) energy density (kcal/100g), (2) protein density (g/100g), and (3) micronutrient/phytonutrient richness. Anchors: 1 = watery fruiting veg with low cal/protein and thin micro profile; 3 = typical root, allium, or moderate berry/fruit; 5 = calorie-dense nuts/seeds or legumes/greens with high protein and exceptional vitamin/mineral density. kcalPer100g and proteinGPer100g are USDA FoodData Central (or SR Legacy) raw edible portion values where available; score is not a linear transform of kcal alone.

crops.biomassNote: total plant fresh (tubers+haulm); edible tubers typically 3–4 kg/m² intensive (Fryd 3–5; French microfarm ~2.4)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Good K, vitamin C, B6; staple energy crop

crops.climateNotes: Excellent CZ fit; haulm frost-killed by autumn frost; plant after soil >8°C; earlies after mid-April lowlands
crops.yieldVariability: Moderate; drought at tuber set cuts yield; late blight risk wet summers
sources: Morel et al. 2017 French microfarm MERLIN (Agric. Syst.)
USDA FDC: Potatoes, flesh and skin, raw

crops.climateNotes: Fully hardy CZ outdoor; prefers cool germination; storage types overwinter in ground or clamp

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Folate, Mn, nitrates; betalain pigments; greens add Fe/vit A

crops.climateNotes: Very good CZ fit; light frost tolerant; bolt risk if sown too early then hot

crops.biomassNote: aboveground at harvest; edible head mid ~5.5 kg/m² (Fryd head cabbage 5–8)

crops.season: spring or summer transplant, summer–autumn harvest

crops.yieldVariability: Cabbage white / clubroot; water stress splits heads

crops.climateNotes: Outstanding CZ winter crop; sweetens after frost; hardy to hard freezes

crops.growthCycleNote: transplant to first ripe fruit (~120–140 d from sow); outdoor harvest window short
crops.biomassNote: aboveground vine+fruit; outdoor edible fruit mid ~5 kg/m² (Fryd outdoor lower end of 4–25; greenhouse MERLIN classic ~12 — do not use for outdoor)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Lycopene, vitamin C, K; low energy density

cozasadit.cz Ice Saints / outdoor tomato guidance

crops.growthCycleNote: transplant to first harvest; continuous fruiting ~60–80 d
crops.biomassNote: vine+fruit season total; edible fruit mid ~5 kg/m² (Fryd courgette 4–6; MERLIN squash ~3.4)

crops.climateNotes: Good CZ summer crop after frosts; frost-sensitive; productive in warm summers

crops.biomassNote: vine+fruit; outdoor edible mid ~4 kg/m² (Fryd 4–25 greenhouse-heavy — outdoor nearer low end)

crops.climateNotes: Outdoor possible CZ but prefers warm nights; downy mildew common; cold frame helps

crops.growthCycleNote: transplant to first colored fruit; outdoor often truncated
crops.biomassNote: plant+fruit; outdoor edible mid ~2 kg/m² (marginal vs Fryd greenhouse 5–15; MERLIN sweet pepper ~3.6 often protected)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Outstanding vitamin C (esp. ripe); carotenoids when colored

crops.climateNotes: MARGINAL outdoor CZ except warmest lowlands/south walls; needs long heat; tunnel strongly recommended; frost-kill
crops.yieldVariability: Very high outdoors — cool summers yield poorly; fruit often harvested green

crops.growthCycleNote: sow/transplant to head or full leaf harvest (cut types shorter)
crops.biomassNote: one succession aboveground; edible mid ~2.5 kg/m² (Fryd ~3; MERLIN ~2.6); multiple successions/year possible

crops.climateNotes: Excellent cool-season CZ crop; bolts in midsummer heat; light frost OK for many cvs

crops.growthCycleNote: sow to first cut; spring or autumn crop

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Exceptional folate, vitamin A/K, Fe, Mg; high protein for leaves

crops.climateNotes: Classic CZ cool crop; overwinter possible mild years; bolts rapidly in long warm days

crops.growthCycleNote: sow to green pod/pea harvest
crops.biomassNote: vines+pods; edible shelled peas or whole pods mid ~1.5 kg/m² peas-in-pod (Fryd peas 2–4; MERLIN pea ~1.1)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Good plant protein, fiber, folate, vitamin C, K; N-fixer

crops.climateNotes: Excellent early CZ crop; frost-tolerant seedlings; heat ends season
crops.yieldVariability: Birds, powdery mildew, uneven flowering in drought

crops.growthCycleNote: sow to first snap-pod harvest; successive picks ~30–40 d
crops.biomassNote: plants+pods; edible snap pods mid ~1.5 kg/m² (Fryd bush beans 1–2)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Vitamin C, K, folate; modest protein fresh; N-fixer

crops.season: May–Jun sow after frost, Jul–Aug harvest
crops.climateNotes: Frost-sensitive; sow after Ice Saints; reliable CZ summer legume
crops.yieldVariability: Moderate; cold wet soils rot seed; aphids/anthracnose

crops.growthCycleNote: spring sow to shelled harvest (~180–220 d autumn-sown overwinter)
crops.biomassNote: haulm+pods; edible shelled beans mid ~1.0–1.2 kg/m² fresh (range uncertain — provisional)

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: High protein/folate for a fresh legume; Fe, Mn; N-fixer; favism caution (G6PD)

crops.climateNotes: Excellent cool CZ legume; more frost-tolerant than Phaseolus; chocolate spot in wet years
crops.yieldVariability: Aphids (black bean), chocolate spot; heat reduces set
sources: USDA FDC: Broadbeans (fava), immature seeds, raw (approx.)

crops.growthCycleNote: perennial: days ≈ annual productive cycle; first meaningful harvest typically year 2 (~400–500 d from plant); June-bearer peak ~20–35 d
crops.biomassNote: annual fruit+runner biomass framing; edible fruit mid ~1.5 kg/m² (MERLIN strawberry ~1.5); not standing crown biomass

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: High vitamin C, Mn, polyphenols; low calorie

crops.season: Aug–Sep plant, May–Jun main harvest (everbearers longer)
crops.climateNotes: Excellent CZ fit; blossom frost risk in late April–May; mulch and fleece help
crops.yieldVariability: Botrytis in wet blossom; frost on open flowers; bed age declines after year 3–4
sources: MZe ČR fruit calendar; pestik.cz strawberry care

crops.growthCycleNote: perennial shrub: days to first meaningful harvest ~2 years; thereafter annual pick window ~14–21 d
crops.biomassNote: annual fruit yield under canopy mid ~1.0–1.2 kg/m² (~10–12 t/ha; Russian cvs trials ~11 t/ha); not woody standing biomass

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Exceptional vitamin C; anthocyanins, K; strong food-forest micronutrient crop

crops.climateNotes: Native-fit to cool CZ/Central Europe; chilling requirement met; late spring frost can hit flowers
crops.yieldVariability: Moderate; gall mite / reversion virus; bird predation
sources: Sazonov et al. ISHS Rubus/Ribes (Russian cvs ~11 t/ha)

crops.growthCycleNote: perennial tree: days to first meaningful harvest ~3 years on dwarfing rootstock (range 2–5); thereafter annual crop

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Fiber, vitamin C (skin), polyphenols; low protein; staple fruit calories

crops.season: dormant plant, Aug–Oct harvest by cv
crops.climateNotes: Core CZ orchard species; cultivars for zones 5–6 abundant; blossom frost risk; fire blight / scab management

sources: Intensive apple orchard yield literature (~40–50 t/ha)
USDA FDC: Apples, raw, with skin
Bulgarian/EU fruit stats context (lower extensive yields)

crops.growthCycleNote: perennial tree: days to first meaningful harvest ~3–5 years; thereafter annual
crops.biomassNote: annual fruit mid ~2.5 kg/m² (25 t/ha good commercial; often lower than apple); not standing wood

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Fiber, vitamin C, copper; similar energy profile to apple

crops.growthCycleNote: perennial multi-stem shrub/small tree: days to first meaningful harvest ~4–5 years (range 4–7); thereafter annual
crops.biomassNote: annual in-shell nut yield mature planting mid ~0.2–0.3 kg/m² (~2–3 t/ha good; high-density trials ~2–3 t/ha); kernel edible fraction of in-shell ~0.4 — biomass is in-shell

nutrientQuality.micronutrientNotes: Very high energy + plant protein; vitamin E, Mg, Mn, healthy fats — top score staple

crops.climateNotes: Excellent CZ fit; prefers cool summers; winter cane damage in exposed sites; virus/phytophthora in wet soils
